risk_reasons: Outbox recovery and tenant-scoped terminal transitions can strand or incorrectly fail an Operator turn.
Staging verification exercises real worker generation with designated synthetic data.
goal: Owner Operator turns recover or fail truthfully under dispatch exhaustion and predecessor waiting, with the next-draft and pinned-location checkpoint demonstrated on staging.
non_goals: Run E operations, restore, refusal lanes or migrations
Changes to the generic watchdog window
A new queue, scheduler, waiting status, provider or dependency
Naming a COO pilot owner or observation window
External Claude or Opus development and review delegates
user_visible_behavior: A turn whose dispatch budget is exhausted stops preparing and shows a dispatch_exhausted failure with a recovery action.
A turn waiting behind its predecessor releases its claim and delays the same job without spending retry budget; healthy waits do not trigger redundant watchdog dispatch.
A staging tone Apply changes the next generated draft for that location.
A staging turn submitted for a secondary location keeps that target when the selector changes.

A staging observation records p50/p95 and justifies the lease, stall and wait constants. The owner explicitly ended the original full-day requirement early on 2026-09-14; preserve the measured duration, all24 submissions, and that authorization without claiming24-hour coverage.
invariants: Accepted turn failure and the winning outbox terminal transition commit or roll back together.

A valid nonterminal turn retains a recoverable outbox unless both terminalize atomically; live or contended claims defer exhaustion, expired claims are revalidated under lock, and stale attempts, foreign accounts and terminal results are preserved.
Outbox ownership and the turn attempt token fence predecessor-wait writes.
A crash during or after waiting remains recoverable by BullMQ or the existing watchdog.
No settings write or public posting occurs from sending a turn; Apply remains separately authorized.
Stored location_id owns the turn target; browser selection never retargets accepted work.
All LLM work stays on the worker and uses the existing cost guard and accounting seam.
No production flag flip or migration; production remains disabled.
edge_cases: Redis reports dispatch failure after accepting a job; a live running turn retains a dispatched outbox, and a later crash is terminalized atomically after its lease expires.
A turn locked by completion defers exhaustion without deadlock or treating contention as absence.
A stale dispatch callback loses its attempt CAS and writes no turn failure.
Watchdog exhaustion of an accepted waiting turn is coupled to its failure.
Healthy predecessor waits cross the old 15-minute age without a watchdog reclaim.
A superseded outbox attempt or stolen turn token cannot refresh liveness or release another claim.
Delay scheduling failure or worker crash leaves durable work recoverable.
The predecessor stall deadline still fails a permanently stuck successor.
No 24-hour result is inferred from a shorter sample. The owner-approved early close uses the actual measured interval and all24 recorded submissions.
